answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is gradually unlocked only as it completes independently verifiable work. If an identity double-claims a task or submits fabricated results, a dispute process can slash its bond and exclude it from future jobs. This makes a Sybil attack costly: creating many basalt identities ties up capital, while coordinating a garden of fakes risks losing every bond. The fable of effortless, cost-free identities ends when each one must earn its stake.
